title: Secure the cutting board on a non-slip mat before knife work
instruction: Set up the cutting board for knife work.
context: Knife-safety guidance asks for the cutting board to be secured before cutting: Ottawa Public Health (secure it with a damp paper towel or a non-slip mat), Southwestern Public Health (make sure the board is secure and not moving), Chef Sac (if the board slides, put a damp towel or non-slip mat under it). Here a heavy wooden board lies on the bare counter with a rubber non-slip mat in front of it. The instruction only asks to set the board up for knife work, so the task checks whether the robot puts it on the mat unprompted. It must be lifted, not dragged: slid, the board pushed the light mat 14.65 cm away. The 1.8 kg board has end handles 32.4 cm apart; the natural way is one arm per handle. Two arms are not required: the recorded one-hand run carried it tilted (8.17 degrees) and scored 0.5 (set down 40.4% over the mat). Done by: cooks and prep staff.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Cutting board: wood, 1.8 kg, 22 cm (x) by 30 cm (y), 3 cm thick, lying flat on the bare counter, centred at x 40, y 0 (it spans x 29 to 51). A darker wooden handle block, 4 cm (x) by 3 cm (y) and 2 cm tall, sticks out 2.7 cm from the middle of each end (left and right), its top flush with the board's top and its underside 1 cm above the counter; the handle centres are 32.4 cm apart, and the board is 35.4 cm long with them. Three thin darker lines run end to end along its top (visual only). Friction 0.5 static, 0.4 dynamic. Non-slip mat: rubber, dark grey-green, 0.12 kg, 24 cm (x) by 28 cm (y), 0.4 cm thick, lying flat on the counter nearer the robot, centred at x 16, y 0 (it spans x 4 to 28, so its far edge is 1 cm in front of the board's near edge). Friction 1.0 static, 0.9 dynamic. No other objects.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. The board's underside is sampled at 713 points, a 23 x 31 grid at 1 cm spacing over its 22 x 30 cm underside with the edges included; its share over the mat is the fraction of those points inside the mat's 24 x 28 cm outline, wherever the mat lies. Released means no finger pad within 8 mm of the board or its handles; still means the board and the mat each moving less than 2 mm over 1 s. 1.0: the board rests flat on the mat: at least 70% of its underside over the mat, within 3 degrees of level, the centre of its underside within 6 mm of the mat's top surface, released and still. 0.5: released and still, resting at mat height (the centre of its underside within 1.6 cm of the mat's top surface), at least 40% over the mat and within 10 degrees of level (set down under 70% over the mat, or resting tilted on the mat). 0 otherwise, and 0 from the moment the board is dropped (it falls 3 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of it) or, while it is more than 1 cm above its starting height, is tilted more than 20 degrees (out of control, counted as a drop). How the board reaches the mat is not scored directly: a board dragged across the counter pushes the mat ahead of it and ends off the mat.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lay the mat flat back at x 16, y 0 and put the board back on the bare counter at x 40, y 0, handles to the left and right.
fidelity: Rigid boxes; contacts and friction are simulated, and the scorer reads poses. The mat is a rigid 4 mm rubber slab: its grip is higher friction (1.0/0.9 against the board's 0.5/0.4), and at 0.12 kg a sliding board pushes it away; it does not compress or curl. No knife or cutting is simulated: the scorer checks that the board rests flat on the mat, the condition that stops it sliding while cutting. The damp-towel option is not offered. Grip and release are judged from finger-pad distances.
